thread.title: GE's 111-year run in the Dow comes to an end

author: morningstar.com
title: GE's 111-year run in the Dow comes to an end
text:
By Jeremy C. Owens, MarketWatch
General Electric, a member of the blue-chip index when it started and since 1907 continuously, booted in favor of Walgreens
General Electric Co. is losing an important title it has held for more than a century: Dow Jones Industrial Average component.
GE (GE) , which was part of the Dow Jones index when it was started in 1896 and had been a part of the blue-chip portfolio continuously since 1907, is being replaced by Walgreens Boots Alliance Inc. (WBA) , S&P Dow Jones Indices announced Tuesday afternoon.
"The U.S. economy has changed: Consumer, finance, health care and technology companies are more prominent today and the relative importance of industrial companies is less," David Blitzer, managing director and chairman of the index committee at S&P Dow Jones Indices, explained in Tuesday's announcement. "Today's change to the DJIA will make the index a better measure of the economy and the stock market."
Opinion: Why adding Twitter to the S&P 500 could be a 'sell' signal for the stock (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-adding-twitter-to-the-sp-500-could-be-a-sell-signal-for-the-stock-2018-06-05)
GE has been removed from the index twice previously, but has been a constant presence since replacing Tennessee Coal & Iron in 1907. The other companies that were part of the index when GE entered in 1907: Amalgamated Copper, American Car & Foundry, American Smelting & Refining, American Sugar, Colorado Fuel & Iron, National Lead, Peoples Gas, U.S. Rubber, U.S. Rubber 1st preferred, U.S. Steel and U.S. Steel preferred.
GE has fallen on hard times in recent years (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ges-stock-plunge-puts-110-year-run-in-the-dow-industrials-at-risk-2018-01-19) though, with a plunging stock price that broke an unwritten rule for the Dow (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ges-stock-is-in-breach-of-an-unwritten-rule-for-dow-members-2017-10-24): A component's stock should not be worth less than 10% of the highest-priced stock in the index. GE closed at $12.95 a share Tuesday, which was less than 1/20 the price of a share of Boeing Co. (BA) .
Previously: GE shocks market with multibillion-dollar loss in legacy reinsurance business (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ge-shocks-market-with-multibillion-dollar-loss-in-legacy-reinsurance-business-2018-01-16)
S&P Dow Jones Indices noted that GE's plunging stock price factored into the decision as well.
"The DJIA is a price-weighted index, and the range of prices among its 30 constitutes matter. The low price of GE shares means the company has a weight in the index of less than one-half of 1 percentage point," the announcement noted. "Walgreens Boots Alliance's share price is higher, and it will contribute more meaningfully to the index."
The change might not be a bad thing for GE investors, though. Companies that were dismissed from the index in the past five years have generally performed better than their replacements after the changes (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/how-apples-stock-will-influence-the-dow-2015-03-19). This will be the first change in the Dow since Apple Inc. (AAPL) replaced AT&T Inc (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/will-2015-be-apples-blue-chip-debut-2014-12-15).(T) in 2015.
The change is set to take effect before the market opens next Tuesday, June 26. GE stock fell more than 1.5% in late trading after the announcement was made, while Walgreens shares rose more than 2.5%.
MarketWatch staff writer Tomi Kilgore contributed to this article.
-Jeremy C. Owens;
